new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the last syllable of the stem: in nouns, adjectives and other non-verbs (which have essentially no post-stem inflection) this is the word-final syllable; in verbs it is the final syllable of the verb stem, with all inflectional suffixes (inverse, plural, perfect, dependent markers) unstressed. Prefixes never affect stress; compounds stress the last syllable of the second root; enclitics are unstressed. Stress is non-contrastive, realized as higher pitch and greater intensity.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In a trisyllabic word the first syllable takes secondary stress and the last primary (132); if the third syllable is a suffix, primary on the second and no secondary (133); when two or three suffix syllables follow the stem, the word-final syllable carries secondary stress while the stem-final syllable keeps primary (127, 134); with noun plural -tëjk the (stressed) suffix is preceded by a secondarily stressed penult (fn. 13). Author notes other Mixe languages show a similar 'competition between the first and the last syllable'.
new_statements.exceptions: Noun plural suffix -tëjk receives primary stress (128); diminutive -u'unk (historically 'child') does not, which distinguishes diminutive suffixation from noun 'child' in composition (129-130); clitics (=a INT, =ëk hearsay) never stressed (131). Convergent statements for the other varieties under this glottocode: Tlahuitoltepec proper (Lyon 1980:33) 'la sílaba tónica de la palabra es la sílaba del radical' except certain always-tonic verbal suffixes; Tamazulápam (Santiago Martínez 2015:53-58) final/iambic in monomorphemic words with tonic ('heavy') vs atonic ('light') suffix classes.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the morphological stem (root + derivation/compounding), right edge; inflectional suffixes and enclitics lie outside it, so verb forms surface with penult/antepenult word-level stress. Examples are citation forms of single words; no phrase-level conditioning described.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Ayutla variety (San Pedro y San Pablo Ayutla, 'Tukyo'm Ayuujk'), which Glottolog The eponymous Santa María Tlahuitoltepec variety is described first-hand by Lyon 1980 (ALIM 8) p.33, saved and read: accent non-contrastive, 'la sílaba tónica de la palabra es la sílaba del radical' except certain always-tonic verbal suffixes — the same root/stem-based rule (note Lyon's p.34 footnote that his accent exposition is adapted from Crawford's Totontepec framework). Tamazulápam (Santiago Martínez 2015 §2.7, also under tlah1239) is likewise final/iambic with tonic vs atonic suffix classes. 'Yacochi Tlahuitoltepec' (Martínez García 2010, penult stress, 9 vowels) is a Totontepec-type North Highland variety spoken inside Tlahuitoltepec municipality and should not be conflated with tlah1239.

sources.note: p.80: 'Except in verbs, the stress is word final. In verbs... the last syllable of the verb stem is stressed'; stress = higher pitch + greater intensity, not contrastive; prefixes irrelevant; inflectional suffixes, diminutive -u'unk and clitics unstressed; noun plural -tëjk takes stress; compounds stress last syllable of 2nd root; secondary stress on 1st syllable of trisyllables, or on word-final syllable when 2-3 suffixes follow the stem (pp. 81-83).

sources.note: p.53-54 (Tamazulápam variety): 'El acento en MTM no es contrastivo... En palabras monomorfémicas el acento siempre en yámbico, es decir, en todo momento cae en la última sílaba'; prefixes never stressed; verbs/nouns: 'heavy' (tonic) suffixes take final stress, 'light' (atonic) suffixes are invisible so the root keeps stress (can yield antepenult); calls MTM 'lengua de acento yámbico y morfológico'; notes Lyon 1980 saw tonic/atonic suffixes in Tlahuitoltepec; contrasts with penult (trochaic) stress in Totontepec/Metepec/Yacochi.

sources.note: p.33 (Tlahuitoltepec proper), verbatim: 'En el sistema fonémico del mixe de Tlahuitoltepec el valor funcional del acento es mínimo. Hasta la fecha no hemos encontrado ningún ejemplo de contraste. Sin embargo, el acento es fonémico en tanto que no es posible predecir cuál sílaba de la palabra será la tónica. Esta bien puede ser la primera, como cyó·ʔnmʌtʌ ‘ellos salieron también’; la última, como en kuhúp ‘sombrero’; o bien puede encontrarse en medio, como en paʌhkstʌ ‘siguen’. Con excepción de ciertos sufijos verbales que siempre son tónicos, la sílaba tónica de la palabra es la sílaba del ra…
